what: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
title: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
text: colortheme lightweight R package providing unified interface managing, customizing, applying qualitative, sequential, diverging color themes. acts versatile bridge base R graphics, custom color definitions, popular palette collections (grDevices, viridisLite, RColorBrewer, khroma, etc.), offering seamless scale integration ggplot2.

title: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
text: Unified Dispatcher (colortheme()): Effortlessly retrieve registered themes name, build themes color vectors functions, modify existing themes fly. Compact Query Syntax: Customize themes instantly using query strings (e.g., reversing order _r, specifying types @qual, adjusting transparency missing-value colors ?alpha=0.5;na.color='gray'). Dual Functional Interface: Extract discrete palette functions ($palette(n)) continuous color ramp functions ($ramp(x)) theme. Base R Data Mapping (map_to_colors()): Directly map discrete continuous vectors hexadecimal color codes base R plots. Seamless ggplot2 Scales: Automatically apply discrete continuous scales using scale_color_theme() scale_fill_theme(), complete proper midpoint handling diverging palettes.

title: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
text: colorthemes() helps find color theme. can filter registry name, source, type using case-insensitive prefix matching. find theme, colortheme() serves central interface load use . can retrieve pre-defined palettes apply compact query syntax reverse colors, change types, inject options.
code: library(colortheme)  # Find color themes matching "ma" colorthemes("ma") #>      name      source       type #> 1 managua      khroma  diverging #> 2 Magenta   grDevices sequential #> 3   magma viridisLite sequential #> 4    mako viridisLite sequential #> 5    Mako   grDevices sequential  # Find color themes from a specific source colorthemes(source = "grDevices") |> head(5) #>         name    source      type #> 1   ArmyRose grDevices diverging #> 2     Berlin grDevices diverging #> 3   Blue-Red grDevices diverging #> 4 Blue-Red 2 grDevices diverging #> 5 Blue-Red 3 grDevices diverging library(colortheme)  # Retrieve a built-in sequential theme and generate colors ct <- colortheme("Viridis") ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#4B0055" "#00588B" "#009B95" "#53CC67" "#FDE333" ct$ramp(seq.int(0, 1, length.out = 5)) #> [1] "#4B0054" "#00578A" "#009B94" "#53CC66" "#FDE333"  # Use query syntax for on-the-fly modifications ct_custom <- colortheme("grDevices/Zissou 1_r@qual?alpha=0.75") ct_custom$palette(4L) #> [1] "#F5191CBF" "#E8A419BF" "#9FC095BF" "#3B99B1BF"

title: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
text: Using as_palette() as_ramp(), can easily extract clean color-generating functions custom graphics workflows.
code: # Extract a discrete palette function taking n pal <- as_palette("Okabe-Ito") pal(6L) #> [1] "#000000" "#E69F00" "#56B4E9" "#009E73" "#F0E442" "#0072B2"  # Extract a continuous ramp function taking x in [0, 1] ramp <- as_ramp("bluescale") ramp(c(0, 0.5, 1.0)) #> [1] "#132B43" "#326A97" "#55B1F7"

what: 3. Direct Mapping for Base R Graphics (map_to_colors())
title: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
text: map_to_colors() automatically handles factor/character variables (qualitative) numeric vectors (sequential/diverging) proper scaling NA management.
code: # Continuous mapping (Sequential) par(mfrow = c(1L, 2L)) plot(cars, col = map_to_colors(cars$speed), pch = 19) plot(cars, col = map_to_colors(cars$speed, "Viridis_r"), pch = 19) # Discrete mapping (Qualitative) plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width,      col = map_to_colors(iris$Species), pch = 19) plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width,      col = map_to_colors(iris$Species, "Set 2"), pch = 19)

title: Unified Color Theme Management and Scales for R Graphics
text: scale_color_theme() automatically detects whether theme qualitative continuous, configuring appropriate ggplot2 scales hood. Diverging themes automatically leverage scales::rescale_mid() midpoint specified.
code: library(ggplot2)  # Qualitative scale ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) +   geom_point(size = 3) +   scale_color_theme("Okabe-Ito_r") # Continuous diverging scale with custom midpoint ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +   geom_tile() +   scale_fill_theme("Cividis", middle = 0.017)

title: Color Themes for Graphics — colortheme
text: "colortheme" object list-like structure provides two primary color-generating functions: $palette() $ramp(). $palette(n) takes integer n returns character vector n discrete colors. primarily intended qualitative themes, distinct colors represent categorical data. $ramp(x) takes numeric vector x values [0, 1] interval returns character vector corresponding colors. maps numeric values onto continuous color gradient, making suitable sequential diverging themes. colortheme() dispatches based class object: object character string (e.g., "Viridis", "grDevices/RdBu_r@q?alpha=.5"), parsed according theme name syntax loaded registry. object color kernel (character vector colors, palette function, ramp function), new color theme constructed. object already "colortheme" object, modified copy returned updated settings.

title: Color Themes for Graphics — colortheme
text: retrieving registered theme string, can use compact URL-like syntax specify source apply --fly modifications: "[(source)/](name)[_r][@(type)][?(query)]" source: (optional) source package collection (e.g., "grDevices"). name: name theme (e.g., "RdBu"). "_r": (optional) suffix reverse color order. type: (optional) desired theme type, matched "sequential", "diverging", "qualitative" (abbreviations like "s", "d", "q" "seq", "div", "qual" supported). query: (optional) key-value pairs separated ; & (e.g., "?alpha=0.5;na.color='gray50'") override theme metadata, options, kernel.args.

title: Color Themes for Graphics — colortheme
code: # Retrieve a pre-defined theme ct <- colortheme("Mako") print(ct) #> Sequential Color Theme: 'Mako' #>  #> Kernel Class: palette #>  #> Options: #>  kernel.size      : Inf #>  reverse.method   : "kernel.args$rev <- !kernel.args$rev" #>  palette.formatter: "interpolate" #>  palette.reverse  : FALSE #>  ramp.rescaler    : c(0, 1) #>  na.color         : NA #>  #> Kernel Arguments: #>  palette: "Mako" #>  alpha  : NULL #>  rev    : FALSE  ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#070707" "#423460" "#007FA8" "#48C2B4" "#E0F7E1" ct$ramp(seq.int(0, 1, length.out = 5)) #> [1] "#060606" "#42345F" "#007FA7" "#48C2B3" "#DFF7E0"  # Use special syntax to get a reversed, qualitative theme with alpha ct <- colortheme("grDevices/Zissou 1_r@qual?alpha=0.75") ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#F5191CBF" "#E78F0ABF" "#EACB2BBF" "#7CBA96BF" "#3B99B1BF"  # Create a new theme from a vector of colors ct <- colortheme(c("#003f5c", "#7a5195", "#ef5675", "#ffa600")) ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#003F5B" "#614D86" "#B85485" "#F46C63" "#FFA500"  # Modify an existing theme ct <- colortheme(ct, type = "qualitative", reverse = TRUE) ct$palette(5L) #> [1] "#ffa600" "#ef5675" "#7a5195" "#003f5c" "#ffa600"

title: List and Register Color Themes — colorthemes
text: colorthemes() extracts metadata registry environment structures data frame, allowing users discover themes name, source, type (case-insensitive prefix matching). register_colortheme() takes color vector, color-generating function, existing "colortheme" object registers specified name source (defaulting "custom/newtheme"). keep registry lightweight, kernel argument supports lazy loading: pass character vector list length 2 first element R expression returning kernel (e.g., "rainbow") second namespace (e.g., "grDevices").

title: List and Register Color Themes — colorthemes
code: # List all available themes head(colorthemes()) #>            name    source      type #> 1      ArmyRose grDevices diverging #> 2        Berlin grDevices diverging #> 3      Blue-Red grDevices diverging #> 4    Blue-Red 2 grDevices diverging #> 5    Blue-Red 3 grDevices diverging #> 6 Blue-Yellow 2 grDevices diverging  # Case-insensitive prefix matching colorthemes(name = "ma") #>      name      source       type #> 1 managua      khroma  diverging #> 2 Magenta   grDevices sequential #> 3    Mako   grDevices sequential #> 4   magma viridisLite sequential #> 5    mako viridisLite sequential  # Register a custom theme register_colortheme(   kernel = c("#264653", "#2a9d8f", "#e9c46a", "#f4a261", "#e76f51"),   name = "sand", source = "custom", type = "sequential" ) colorthemes(name = "sand") #>   name source       type #> 1 sand custom sequential  # Remove the custom theme by passing NULL register_colortheme(NULL, name = "sand", source = "custom")
